item.title: Shimonoseki Fugu Festival — Guide
item.description: As Japan’s fugu capital, Shimonoseki celebrates its signature blowfish with seasonal festivals and events, especially as the fugu season peaks in autumn and winter. These gatherings — held at the port, markets and temples — bring together fugu tastings and cheap eats, market stalls, and even Shinto rituals giving thanks for the harvest and praying for safety, reflecting the fish’s deep importance to the city. For visitors, a fugu festival is a lively, affordable and atmospheric way to enjoy the delicacy alongside locals, sampling fugu dishes at their seasonal best in the very city that made them famous.

item.title: Sapporo Autumn Fest Guide: Hokkaido Food Festival (Sep)
item.description: Every September, Odori Park fills with the smells of grilling seafood, sizzling meat and fresh produce for the Sapporo Autumn Fest (Sapporo Autumn Festival) — a glorious celebration of Hokkaido’s harvest and one of Japan’s great food events. For several weeks, the park’s blocks become themed gourmet zones showcasing the bounty of the island: crab and scallops, ramen, jingisukan, soup curry, dairy, sweets, sake and local wine, region by region. With long tables, autumn weather and the whole island’s cuisine in one place, it’s a food lover’s dream and a delicious way to round off summer.
